C0.quote: deals with iterative voting under the plurality rule
C0.note: Strategic and computational aspects of plurality iterative voting.

C1.quote: exploring the computational complexity of determining possible and necessary iterative winners
C1.note: Results: complexity (Thm 5.2, 5.3), probabilistic bounds on equilibrium (IAC/IC), Condorcet efficiency, small simulation. Primary is AL as a judgment call; probabilistic analysis is spread across types.

C2.1.value: preference profile; ballot profile; truthful ballot
C2.1.quote: Let bi ∈ M denote the ballot submitted by voter i

C2.2.quote: represented by a linear order ≻i over candidates
C2.2.note: Plurality ballots are single candidates (top choice), derived from linear order preferences; the held attitudes are strict rankings.

C2.3.quote: Each voter i ∈ N has preferences over candidates

C2.4.quote: Let b⊤ denote the truthful ballot profile
C2.4.note: Ballots b_i and preferences ≻_i have separate notation; ballots can deviate from truthful.

C3.1.quote: how frequently the initial ballot profile is already an equilibrium
C3.1.note: Iterative analyses involve strategic deviations; the analysis of the truthful initial plurality winner (Condorcet efficiency baseline) is non-strategic.

C3.2.note: Initial profile is truthful by assumption; the Condorcet efficiency of plain plurality is evaluated on truthful ballots.

C3.3.quote: we examine the classical iterative voting model introduced by Meir et al. [22]
C3.3.note: Truthful start is part of the classical model cited; no incentive argument given.

C4.1.note: Social welfare is mentioned only in related work about other papers; the paper itself uses no utility notions for voters.

C5.1.quote: Condorcet efficiency (CE) is defined as the probability of electing
C5.1.note: Condorcet efficiency as a quality criterion for outcomes; it is a majority-based criterion rather than one of the listed ones. Judged borderline and coded Y as an evaluation of outcome quality.

C5.2.note: Condorcet winner is computed from preferences ≻ (held), compared to the winner from ballots; Condorcet winner is defined on the held preference profile, so it is evaluated on held attitudes.

VOT.quote_behav: voters perform direct best responses when they are pivotal
VOT.quote_info: if i believes that voting for y will make candidate y the new winner
VOT.note: Best responses are computed with respect to the current score vector, which implies knowledge of the current scores.

C8.1.quote: We then consider a best response dynamics

C8.2.quote: iterative voting under the plurality rule
C8.2.note: Iterative voting / best response dynamics named explicitly.

claims.quote: Condorcet efficiency of plurality is increased by considering its iterative voting version
our analysis also helps provide theoretical insights on how beneficial manipulation can be

C9.1.note: Claims about the benefit of manipulation and the quality of the rule.

C9.2.note: The claims need the model of strategic best-response voters with truthful start and the culture assumption (IC/IAC); these are stated. Condorcet winner is defined on held preferences, so no further link is needed.
